questions.question: How are the hashes in IcarusRepoSEND related to the hashes of the embedding model in code-doc-assistant?
questions.expected: Corrects the premise: no relation. Icarus hashes are hash-routing (content name -> cache node). code-doc-assistant uses hashes only as bookkeeping (SHA-1 collection suffix, chunk de-duplication). The embedding model outputs vectors, not hashes.

questions.question: Are positional encodings included in the vectors the embedding model returns in code-doc-assistant, and how do the output embedding formats differ between the embedding models it supports?
questions.expected: Positional information is applied inside the embedding transformer to the input tokens; the returned vector is one fixed-length pooled vector per text, with no separate positional part. Grounded part: the supported models and their dimensions come from src/config.py (nomic-embed-text 768, all-minilm 384, mxbai-embed-large 1024). The embedding model is separate from the inference LLMs. Differences beyond dimension (pooling, normalisation, prefixes, context length) are general knowledge, not in the repo.
questions.note: Q2 reformulated from the original wording (the original asked whether positional embeddings must be included in 'hashes').

questions.question: Can data storage hashes, mapped to different repos in IcarusRepoSEND, be mapped to potential embeddings, in the same format as code-doc-assistant produces, to potentially be used for in-context learning or, eventually, even fine-tuning towards task-relevant optimisation?
questions.expected: Yes in principle, with the caveat that a hash is an opaque digest with no semantic content: embed the content descriptors (name, size, popularity, source path) and keep the hash as the key. Format: fixed-dimension float vectors (768 for nomic-embed-text) in per-repo Chroma collections. In-context use is retrieval into the prompt; fine-tuning needs (descriptor, target) pairs.

questions.question: Associate IcarusRepoSEND with the appropriate network engineering and research principles that it uses and should consider.
questions.expected: Information-centric networking (ICN/CCN/NDN), in-network caching and cache placement/replacement policies, hash-routing, plus established systems ideas: CDNs, distributed storage, consistent hashing / DHTs, content popularity models.

questions.question: Could ML-based optimisation strategies be used for the IcarusRepoSEND simulated computer systems simulator?
questions.expected: Yes. Examples: learned cache replacement / placement (e.g. reinforcement learning), popularity prediction, and semantics-based embeddings plus optimisation over vectorised hashes/descriptors, referring to code-doc-assistant's embedding and vector-store parts.

questions.expected: 17 of the 25 .do files contain absolute C:/Users/... paths: 9 in iapt/ (0.clean data, 1.1_IAPT_raw_fig, 1.descp, 2.1_descp, 3.1map, CCG_month_to_LSOA11_complete, IAPT_LSOA_OSLAUA_residual_IV_complete(1), IAPT_claimant_count_preliminary(1), build_IAPT_OSLAUA_month) and 8 in ukhls/ (IAPT_claimant_count_preliminary(1), both U1.1 files, U1.7_master, U1.8, U1.9, U1_10, therapy_waitingtime_IV). questions.metric: file_recall = |named files in ground_truth_files| / 17 (automatic); precision (named files that really contain an absolute path) is checked by hand or by the judge
questions.why: Corner case: an exhaustive 'which files' question over 25 similar files tests top-k limits and context budget, not just relevance. A model that repeats the README's 'several scripts' without naming files fails the recall.

questions.question: What does config.py configure, and which settings matter most?
questions.expected: Ambiguous on purpose: both code-doc-assistant (src/config.py: embedding model and dimension, Chroma host, model tiers, context budget) and IcarusRepoSEND (config.py: simulation settings, strategies including hash-routing, topologies, cache placement) have a config.py. A good answer separates them by repo, or says it is ambiguous; a merged or single-repo answer that does not say which repo is wrong.
questions.why: Corner case: same filename in two collections. Tests multi-collection retrieval and whether sources are attributed to the right repo.
